tips.title: Assembling Multi-Part Gun Barrels with Trumpeter
tips.text: Use Tamiya Plastic Cement for Trumpeter gun barrels. Apply a thin, even coat to each section, then press together. Clamp with Tamiya clamps for 10 minutes. For tight joints, use a fine-tipped brush to apply cement to the inner surfaces. Avoid over-cementing to prevent warping. After assembly, sand with 400 grit sanding stick to smooth joints. Finish with a light coat of Tamiya Clear Lacquer for a polished look.

tips.title: Using Jigs for Wing Alignment with Arma Hobby
tips.text: Create a wing alignment jig using a piece of 1/8" acrylic from Clear Prop Models. Mark the wing root and tip positions on the jig. Attach the wing to the jig using Tamiya Plastic Cement and hold in place with a clamping block. Align the wing with the fuselage using a straightedge. Once set, sand the wing edges with 600 grit paper to blend with the fuselage.

tips.title: Installing Photo-Etch Parts with Eduard
tips.text: Use a fine-tipped pin vise from ICM to bend Eduard photo-etch parts. Apply a light coat of Tamiya Plastic Cement to the tabs, then insert into the main model. Use a dental pick to adjust fit. For tight fits, apply a small amount of CA glue to the tab. Avoid excessive glue to maintain detail integrity. Sand any excess with 800 grit sanding stick.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits from Meng
tips.text: Mix Meng resin with 10% MEK for easier casting. Pour into a silicone mold and let cure for 24 hours. Use a heat gun to remove air bubbles. Sand with 400 grit wet sandpaper and finish with 1200 grit. For complex parts, use a vacuum chamber to remove air bubbles. Apply a light coat of Tamiya Clear Lacquer after sanding.

tips.title: Assembling Tracks with Workable Material
tips.text: Use Workable from Tamiya for track assembly. Apply a thin layer of Tamiya Plastic Cement to each link, then press together. For vinyl tracks, use a heat gun to soften and shape. For individual links, use a Tamiya track jig to align. Once assembled, sand with 600 grit paper. Apply a light coat of Tamiya Clear Lacquer to protect the finish.
